title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 160 (Return of goods bailed, on expiration of time or accomplishment of purpose)

content.overview: Section 160 provides that it is the duty of the bailee to return, or deliver according to the bailor’s directions, the goods bailed, without demand, as soon as the time for which they were bailed has expired, or the purpose for which they were bailed has been accomplished.
content.glance: Bailee must return or deliver the goods according to the bailor’s directions, without demand, as soon as the time expires or the purpose is accomplished.
content.study: It is the duty of the bailee to return, or deliver according to the bailor’s directions, the goods bailed, without demand, as soon as the time for which they were bailed has expired, or the purpose for which they were bailed has been accomplished. Current-law framing: automatic duty on expiration or accomplishment; no demand required.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: It is the duty of the bailee to return, or deliver according to the bailor’s directions, the goods bailed, without demand, as soon as the time for which they were bailed has expired, or the purpose for which they were bailed has been accomplished.

examples.title: Expiration of time
examples.body: Goods bailed for a fixed period. On expiry, bailee must return them without demand under Section 160.

hypotheticals.question: Purpose of bailment is accomplished. Must the bailee wait for a demand before returning the goods?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 160 requires return or delivery according to directions without demand as soon as the purpose is accomplished.
